name: TLV9064IDR
title: TLV906x 10 MHz rail-to-rail input/output CMOS op amps (single, dual, quad, with shutdown versions)
summary: TLV9061, TLV9062 and TLV9064 are one-, two- and four-channel CMOS op amps for 1.8 V to 5.5 V supplies with rail-to-rail inputs and outputs, 10 MHz gain bandwidth, 6.5 V/µs slew rate and 538 µA quiescent current per amplifier. They are unity-gain stable, drive 100 pF directly and have internal RFI/EMI input filtering. The S versions add active-low shutdown pins that cut supply current to 0.5 µA typical.
key_figures: 10 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz, 16 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz

circuits.title: Single-pole low-pass filter
circuits.description: A non-inverting stage whose input first passes an RC low-pass, R1 into C1 to ground, so the response has one pole at 1/(2π·R1·C1) and a pass-band gain of 1 + RF/RG set by the feedback divider.

circuits.title: Low-side current sense
circuits.description: The load current returns to ground through a 0.1 Ω shunt; the amplifier, on a 5 V supply, takes the shunt voltage on IN+ and amplifies it non-inverting with RF = 165 kΩ and RG = 3.4 kΩ, a gain near 49.5 V/V. Loads from 0 A to 1 A give at most 100 mV across the shunt and about 0 V to 4.95 V at the output.

parts.note: load carrying ILOAD, 0 A to 1 A

circuits.title: Op amp used as an inverting comparator
circuits.description: One channel of a TLV9062 runs open loop on a 5 V supply. Two equal 100 kΩ resistors split the supply to a 2.5 V threshold on IN+, and the 0 V to 5 V input goes to IN–. The output sits at the positive rail while the input is below the threshold and swings to the negative rail when it rises above.

circuits.title: Series resistor limiting input current
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower whose input is driven through a 5 kΩ resistor, so that an input pushed past a supply rail sends no more than 10 mA through the internal clamp diodes. The resistor adds thermal noise at the input.

circuits.title: Two non-inverting stages (layout example)
circuits.description: Both channels of a TLV9062 as non-inverting amplifiers, each with RG from its inverting input to ground and RF from output to inverting input. The layout places RF and RG beside the inverting pin and a low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitor at each supply pin.

operation.text: TLV9061 has one amplifier, TLV9062 two and TLV9064 four; the S versions (TLV9061S, TLV9062S, TLV9064S) add shutdown pins. All are CMOS op amps running from 1.8 V to 5.5 V with inputs and outputs reaching both rails, 10 MHz unity-gain bandwidth, 10 nV/√Hz broadband noise, 0.5 pA bias current, ±0.3 mV typical offset and 538 µA quiescent current per amplifier, specified from -40°C to +125°C.

Each amplifier is stable at unity gain and drives 100 pF directly. Its open-loop output impedance is resistive, which makes larger capacitive loads easier to compensate. RFI and EMI filtering sits inside the inputs, and overdriving an input does not reverse the output phase.
On the TLV906xS devices a low level on SHDN puts the amplifier into standby, where it draws under 1 µA typical.

The common-mode range runs 100 mV past each rail at any supply from 1.8 V to 5.5 V. A P-channel pair handles inputs from 200 mV below V– up to about (V+) – 1.4 V, an N-channel pair handles inputs from about (V+) – 1.4 V to 200 mV above V+, and both conduct in a narrow band, typically (V+) – 1.2 V to (V+) – 1 V. With process spread that band can sit anywhere from (V+) – 1.4 V to (V+) – 0.8 V. Offset, offset drift, PSRR, CMRR and THD are worse inside it.
A class AB output with common-source transistors comes within 15 mV of each rail into 10 kΩ, whatever the supply; other loads change how close it gets.

When the input or gain drives the output past its range, the output transistors saturate; leaving saturation takes about 200 ns, after which the output slews at the normal rate. Delay through an overloaded stage is that recovery time plus the slewing time.

SHDN is a high-impedance CMOS input, active low and referenced to V–. Its threshold is about 800 mV above V– whatever the supply, with hysteresis. Logic low is V– to V– + 0.2 V; logic high is V– + 1.2 V to V+. The pin must be driven or tied to a valid level, never left floating. The dual has one control per amplifier and the quad one per pair. Enable takes 10 µs from full shutdown of all channels and disable 3 µs. A disabled output is high-impedance, so outputs can share a bus or the part can serve as a gated amplifier. Turn-off time grows with load resistance; the specified time needs the 10 kΩ load to mid-supply, and with no load it is much longer.
The amplifiers work from 1.8 V (±0.9 V) to 5.5 V (±2.75 V); many figures are specified from -40°C to 125°C.

With no feedback, the two voltages to compare go straight to the inputs. The input range extends 100 mV past each rail and the output never reverses phase anywhere in that range. Propagation delay is the overload recovery time plus the slewing time; overdrive under 100 mV lengthens it, since recovery slows and the slew rate falls.

More than 6 V across the supply can damage the part permanently. Low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitors go between each supply pin and ground, as close to the part as possible; in single-supply use one capacitor from V+ to ground is enough.

Every pin carries internal ESD protection. On the inputs and output this is mainly steering diodes to the supply pins, which also protect against input overdrive in circuit while the current stays at or below 10 mA. A series resistor in the driven input holds the current down; it adds thermal noise, so it should be small where noise matters.

Keep analog and digital grounds apart and watch where ground current flows; ground planes on one or more layers of a multilayer board spread heat and lower EMI pickup. Route inputs away from supply and output traces, crossing them at 90° when they must cross. Put RF and RG right at the inverting input and keep input traces short. Sensitive traces can be ringed with a guard trace held at low impedance to cut leakage. Clean the board after assembly, and after any aqueous cleaning bake it at 85°C for 30 minutes to drive moisture out of the package.
